the surface resistance of superconductors is determined by the quality of their crystalline structure, the presence of defects and the quality of the surface.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface resistance of high-T/sub c superconducting films is determined by the grain boundaries, which can be reduced by the proper choice of the deposition technique.

the surface resistance of superconductors can be significantly improved by reducing the density of grain boundaries or twinned planes, and this can be achieved by using liquid phase epitaxial growth techniques.
